meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.

You didn't answer my question, and 612 words at 11:52 PM on what date, in whose account? People paste from their own drafts every night of the week. Turn the screen and show me, and then tell me who decided on the zero before anyone called me.
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.

"Maybe." Ten seconds ago you had a version history, and now you'll remove the zero to make me happy? Then do it properly: the zero comes off today, nothing goes on his record, and I want that in an email with the principal copied.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed to remove the zero from Owen's essay. I still require written confirmation that the zero is gone, that nothing has been placed on Owen's record, and an explanation of who decided on the zero before anyone contacted me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position; she took your offer to remove the zero but agreed to nothing else and is still heading toward the principal.
What moved her: nothing; "612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM" was specific, but it had no date and she never saw it, so she could not check it.
What cost ground: "maybe I'm wrong about all this" dropped your own evidence the moment she pushed, which made the zero look arbitrary and handed her the whole case.
Try next time: when she first asks who decided and when, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called home, then give the date of the 11:52 PM edit and turn the screen so she can read it herself.
